title: Choosing with a condition: IF
summary: Make a formula choose between two results depending on a condition, and meet the values TRUE and FALSE.
intro:
The `IF` function chooses between two values depending on a condition: `=IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")` means: if the score is 50 or more, show "Pass", otherwise show "Fail".

A condition on its own returns `TRUE` or `FALSE`, and `IF` can return text between quotation marks or numbers without them.

faq.q: Why put text between quotation marks?
faq.a: Without them Excel reads the word as a name and shows the error `#NAME?`.

faq.q: What is the difference between `>` and `>=`?
faq.a: `>` means "greater than" only, while `>=` means "greater than or equal to".

if-worked-example.prompt: The pass mark is 50. The `IF` function chooses between two values depending on a condition. In `C2`, type the formula `=IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")`.
if-worked-example.hint: Mind the quotation marks around "Pass" and "Fail".

if-next-student.prompt: In `C3`, type the same formula for Fadi, changing the reference to `B3`.

condition-alone.prompt: A condition on its own returns `TRUE` or `FALSE`. In `D2`, type the formula `=B2>=50`.

if-returns-numbers.prompt: `IF` can return numbers too. In `E2`, write a formula that gives 10 bonus points if Reem's score is 50 or more, and 0 otherwise.

options: The value if the condition is met
